title: Branch, push and open a pull request
intro: Your manager asks for refunds to be shown separately. You'll make the change on a **branch**, then push it to GitHub so it can be reviewed.
welcome: You're inside your repository from the last lesson. Type help at any time.

steps.goal: Create a new branch called `add-refunds` and switch to it.
steps.hint: `git switch -c add-refunds` (older guides write `git checkout -b add-refunds`, which does the same).
steps.explain: A branch is a safe copy to work on, like drafting a reply before sending it. `main` stays untouched until your change is approved.

mistakes.say: That works fine in real life! For this exercise, please call it `add-refunds` so the later steps match. Type `git switch -c add-refunds`.
That *creates* the branch but doesn't move you onto it. `git switch -c add-refunds` does both in one go.

steps.goal: We've edited `totals.py` for you (pretend!). Stage the change.

extra.output:
On branch add-refunds
Changes not staged for commit:
	modified:   totals.py

-    return round(sum(amounts), 2)
+    paid = [a for a in amounts if a > 0]
+    return round(sum(paid), 2)

steps.goal: Commit it with a clear message.

mistakes.say: Remember the message in quotes: `git commit -m "Show refunds separately"`.

steps.goal: Connect your folder to your empty GitHub repository. Its address is `https://github.com/you/statement-totals.git`.
steps.hint: `git remote add origin https://github.com/you/statement-totals.git`. *origin* is the usual nickname for your main copy on GitHub.
steps.explain: Git now knows where *origin* is. You only do this once per project.

mistakes.output: fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository
mistakes.say: Git doesn't know where to push yet. Add the remote first.

steps.hint: `git push -u origin add-refunds`. The `-u` remembers the link, so next time `git push` on its own is enough.

steps.explain: Your branch is on GitHub. Next, in the browser, you'd open a **pull request**: a request for someone to review and merge your change into `main`. It works like a refund that needs a second approver.

mistakes.output:
fatal: The current branch add-refunds has no upstream branch.
To push the current branch and set the remote as upstream, use

    git push --set-upstream origin add-refunds
mistakes.say: The first push of a new branch needs to say *where*. Git even printed the fix. You can use the shorter `-u` instead of `--set-upstream`.
That pushes `main`, which hasn't changed. Your work is on `add-refunds`.

finish: Branch → commit → push → pull request. This is how every team you'll join works.
